subject: Evidence of deletion request + temporary log retention exception
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@heliostx.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@heliostx.com
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: deletion attestation + temporary log retention exception

Diego / Kimberly,

Thanks — Helios has completed a data minimization sweep on our side and we need Redwood to provide: 1) a deletion attestation (manifest of records purged and backups removed) for the customer project id HLS-1972, and 2) a short-term exception to your standard log eviction schedule so our security team can complete a regulator-driven investigation (estimated additional hold: 14 days).

Specific asks:
- Deletion manifest CSV with object identifiers (hashed IDs are fine), deletion timestamps, and which storage tier (primary/replica/backup) each entry was removed from.
- Confirmation of backup snapshot purge plan and expected completion date. We understand some snapshots are immutable; if so, please indicate manual purge steps.
- Temporary log retention exception for 14 calendar days starting once you acknowledge — we only need event-level audit logs and request traces for the HLS-1972 tenancy.

I've attached Helios_SoC2_redacted.pdf and a CSV with the identifiers we can share (requested_identifiers.csv).  We can sign any reasonable confidentiality addendum or DSR to enable this. Can you confirm feasibility and a target timeline?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — regulator has a 30-day window.

—Emma Jones
Director, InfoSec
Helios Therapeutics

Attachments: Helios_SoC2_redacted.pdf (PDF), requested_identifiers.csv (CSV)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@heliostx.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: deletion attestation + temporary log retention exception

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Acknowledged.

Quick answers up front: feasible, but we need a short operational window to coordinate backup purges that may touch immutable snapshots and cross-border subprocessor flows.  I'll outline proposed next steps below; Kimberly and Karthik, I'm looping you in for privacy/compliance + legal coverage.

Proposed plan / questions:
- Authorization: Do you want us to accept the attached CSV as the canonical identifier list, or will you provide a signed DSR / addendum? (Legal typically needs a signed request for audit artifacts.)
- Timeline: If we receive signed authorization by EOD Mon (11 Jan), we can produce a draft deletion manifest within 3 business days and target backup purge completion within 14 calendar days after manifest finalization.
- Log exception: We can gate an exception for 14 days limited to HLS-1972 traces. We need the exact log types (auth events, API request traces, or infra metrics) — please confirm the minimum set.
- Subprocessors / transfers: For any backup locations that are handled by subprocessors (cloud providers, backup vendors), we'll list the subprocessor and whether manual purge is required. Cross-border transfers that require export checks may extend timelines by a few days.

I'll prepare a ticket and a data-handling addendum template for your legal team. Can you confirm whether redacted manifests are acceptable (i.e., hashed identifiers instead of PII)?

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@heliostx.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: deletion attestation + temporary log retention exception

Emma — thanks for the context.  Two legal/compliance points to make this operational: 

1) Formal authorization: We require a signed Data Subject Request (DSR) or a brief retention-exception addendum that explicitly references HLS-1972 and authorizes Redwood to hold the specified logs for the stated 14-day period. I'll attach a one-page addendum template to the ticket.

2) Evidence format and scope: We will provide a deletion manifest in CSV format. For security/external reporting purposes we can redact identifiers (SHA256 hashed) — please confirm acceptable fields. Redwood will include: hashed_id, deletion_timestamp_utc, storage_tier (primary|replica|backup), subprocessor_location, and purge_method (automated|manual).

Operational SLAs (for planning):
- Receipt of signed authorization -> draft manifest within 3 business days.
- Manifest review cycle (Helios comments) -> up to 4 business days for finalization.
- Backup snapshot purge: most automated backups will be purged within 7 calendar days after manifest finalization; immutable snapshots or third-party backup vendors may require up to 14 calendar days and manual offboarding.

Note on subprocessors and cross-border transfers: If any backup resides with a subprocessor that performs cross-border processing, we will provide the subprocessor name and country in the manifest and identify whether manual remediation is required. Those cases often add 48-72 hours for approvals.

Please confirm acceptance of the one-page addendum and whether redacted SHA256 identifiers are OK. Once we have that, we'll open an engineering ticket, include SOC2 artifacts, and begin the purge workflow.

—Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, security@heliostx.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: deletion attestation + temporary log retention exception

Karthik / Diego — thanks, that all sounds reasonable. Helios will:
- Sign the one-page retention-exception addendum (we'll return it by EOD Wed 13 Jan).
- Accept SHA256-hashed identifiers in the manifest (redaction confirmed).
- Limit log scope to API request traces and auth events only.

Please proceed to open the engineering ticket and attach the SOC2 artifact to it. For audit continuity, we request the deletion manifest file (CSV) be placed in a secure share (Drive link) and that Redwood retain an internal ticket trail of actions.

We appreciate the clear SLAs — regulator timeline noted.

Emma Jones
Director, InfoSec
Helios Therapeutics
